# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding & first 30 days**: no documented journey from sign-up → first class → retention checkpoint. This is your biggest revenue leakage point.
- **Churn & win-back**: no process for identifying at-risk members, pause protocols, or reactivation campaigns. You're losing revenue passively.
- **Coaching quality & consistency**: Class Quality Audit Checklist missing; no standard for what "good" looks like across all coaches.
- **Complaints & incidents**: no escalation path, documentation standard, or resolution SOP. Liability and member trust gap.
- **Health & safety incident reporting**: no log, no post-incident review, no member communication protocol.
- **Data & GDPR compliance**: no documented data retention, deletion, or consent audit process. Legal/regulatory risk.
- **Member outcomes tracking**: no SOP for measuring/communicating progress (strength, body composition, consistency). Reduces perceived value and retention.
- **Referral programme mechanics**: no rules, tracking, or reward fulfilment process. Leaving easy growth on the table.
- **Finance reconciliation**: unclear if daily/weekly reconciliation of memberships, cancellations, and payments is documented.

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Coaches SOPs (21/24)**: Weekly Key Coach Tasks missing — no documented prep, class setup, member check-in cadence, feedback loops. Likely coaches operate inconsistently.
- **Coaching Development Roadmap missing**: no progression path from new coach → senior/mentor. Affects retention and quality.
- **Client SOPs (28/37)**: Member Checkins, Member Pause, Milestone Achievements, 30 Day Goals, Troubleshooting Guide all absent. These are retention levers you've built the infrastructure for but haven't operationalised.

# Service Menu Build — Tactical Execution for The Forge

• **Start with YOUR pricing reality first** — Don't design what sounds good. List every service you currently deliver (class types, PT sessions, nutrition consults, assessments, etc.), what you're actually charging NOW, and what your margin targets are. This anchors the menu to what works, not wishful thinking. Takes 1 hour max.

• **Build TWO documents, not one** — Members see pricing, inclusions, and benefits in simple language (what problem does each service solve?). Coaches get the INTERNAL version: price points, margins, upsell sequences, contraindications, how to position each offering. They sell differently when they know the "why" behind pricing.

• **Use your current member data to validate gaps** — Pull your last 3 months of sales/bookings. Which services are members actually buying? Which are you *suggesting* but nobody wants? Cut the dead weight, double down on what moves. Update the menu to match reality, not theory.

• **Make it a sales tool, not a brochure** — Include specific outcomes ("6-week strength foundations program = measurable strength gains + confidence to lift independently") and clear next steps for each tier. Coaches should be able to recommend a service path to any new member in 2 minutes.

• **Lock it in a shared system TODAY** — Don't let it live in a Word doc. Put it in your booking software, WhatsApp team channel, or printed in the gym where coaches see it daily. It only works if it's actually *used*.

What's your current pricing spread like across services?

## REVENUE: The core problem—member acquisition stalling, retention volatile, pricing soft

**Last 3 months (Aug–Oct) vs prior 3 (May–Jul):**
- Revenue down 11% (£19,348 avg → £18,650 avg)
- Member count up 26% (131 → 159) but revenue *per member* collapsed 27% (£130 → £112)
- October churn hit 4%—your best—but August spiked to 5.6% and May to 12.8%: retention is inconsistent

**SPECIFIC ACTIONS:**

1. **Raise membership price by £8–12/month immediately.** You're at £118/member (March) trending to £106 (Oct). Competitors' women-only gyms in Belfast run £35–45/month; you're likely at ~£30. Test a £38–42 tier on new joiners this month. Your member base grew 39% (120→167) in 7 months—you've got pricing power. Even 10% uplift = +£1,760/month on current base.

2. **Plug the May churn spike—it was 12.8%, triple your best rate.** Investigate: facility issues post-move? Staff turnover? Run an exit survey on 2026-05 leavers NOW (retroactive). Then lock in a 90-day new-member onboarding sequence (email, check-in call, week-6 progress chat). Target: hold churn at ≤4% (October standard).

3. **Monetise class attendance gaps.** You have 159 members but average revenue/member is £106—implying 25–30% aren't paying full rate or attending regularly. Introduce tiered pricing: "Off-peak" (Mon–Fri 10 a.m.–4 p.m.) at -20%; "Peak+" (5–8 p.m., weekends) at +£5; "Class pack" (10×classes, 12% discount, 6-week expiry) to fill 6 a.m. and noon slots. Quick model: if 20 members buy Class packs at £60 (vs £40/month baseline), that's +£400/month.
